review_type: Independent AI scientific review; not acceptance prediction
summary: A six-configuration, 1,008-image audit separates common prompt response from centered painter contrasts in 31 fixed features and two learned representations. A cross-repeat estimator evaluates finite-reference contrast error; a retrospective held-scene mean translation changes reference-prototype prompt-name recognition while supervised generated centroids perform better. An assumed-covariance analysis quantifies primary-error point-order sensitivity.
recommendation_rationale: Technically coherent and carefully scoped empirical work, with exact replay of the new analyses. The contribution remains too concentrated in a reused four-painter, fixed-prompt, single-session panel to convincingly establish the broader evaluation lesson. Retrospective extensions interpret that panel but do not independently establish generality or actual repeat-error independence. The reservation is empirical importance, not lack of a new algorithm.

strengths.text: Correctly distinguished estimands, artist centering, cross-repeat correction and score identities; signed estimates and finite-target limitations are handled appropriately.

strengths.location: pp. 4-7, Sections 5.2 and 5.6; Appendices I and L
strengths.text: Generic painting control and exact common/labeled prototype-gain decomposition address a real ambiguity in an established similarity measure.
Held-scene exclusion, untuned correction, explicit information budgets, harmful outcomes and stronger supervised comparator are all retained.

strengths.location: Appendices L, M, N and O
strengths.text: Strong provenance and numerical reproducibility. Combined 65 tests pass, both new analyses replay exactly, and all 15 selected science hashes match.

weaknesses.location: pp. 1-2, Introduction and Section 3.1; pp. 6-8, Sections 5.6-7; Appendices L.4 and M.1-M.3
weaknesses.text: Four related painters, one outdoor prompt panel and one session do not establish the reach of the central empirical evaluation lesson. A large shared response may represent legitimate group-level characteristics. The existing sensitivities do not test an independent candidate set or untouched prompt/session panel.

weaknesses.location: p. 2, Section 2; pp. 7-8, Section 5.7; pp. 33-34, Appendix M
weaknesses.text: The common-offset decision diagnostic is an established intercept change, and generated-domain classifier advantages overlap with prior prompted-artist and domain-generalization experiments. Its specific empirical outcomes are useful but retrospective; related work should discuss Su et al.’s classification and generator-domain evidence more directly.

weaknesses.location: p. 4, Section 4.3; p. 15, Appendix C.4; p. 44, Appendix N.5; pp. 45-46, Appendix O
weaknesses.text: Two repeats and contiguous scene blocks cannot identify service covariance or session state. The new sensitivity does not calibrate actual dependence, interval coverage, or headline shared-fraction bias. Honest disclosure prevents overclaiming but does not qualify the sampling model empirically.

weaknesses.location: p. 8, Reproducibility; p. 27, Appendix L.4; pp. 43-45, Appendix N
weaknesses.text: No complete public exact-pixel archive or verified recovery route is supplied, preventing independent measurement-layer reproduction despite strong vector-level replay.

weaknesses.location: pp. 3-8, Sections 4-6 and Tables 1-4; Appendices L-M
weaknesses.text: Many related quantities obscure the main thread. Add a map of baselines, targets, invariances and interpretations, and summarize painter-level transfer gains and source-view exceptions.

questions: What transferable empirical conclusion is intended beyond metric disagreement in this four-painter panel, and what independent-panel result would falsify it?

Does common naming movement primarily encode legitimate characteristics shared by this painter group? A matched movement-level control or second artist group would help distinguish this from a broadly generic response.
Can exact pixels and complete attribution be supplied through an anonymous artifact or verified recovery manifest?
Can the main text summarize painter-level transfer changes and source-view exceptions alongside aggregate original-target gains?
ethics_assessment: No specific ethical violation is evidenced. AI source auditing and incomplete attribution/release packaging are disclosed; the latter is an outstanding release task.

revision_priorities.text: Prospectively test the principal decomposition and decision diagnostic on a second artist/content panel or independently held-out benchmark subset, with a declared empirical hypothesis and adverse outcomes retained.
If inferential repeat correction remains central, collect independently interleaved repeat/session blocks to separate request noise from session variation.
Provide exact-pixel access or verified full recovery with preprocessing, selection and attribution records.
Focus the main narrative, add a quantity map, discuss Su et al.’s classifier/domain results, and highlight reference-view exceptions.
